column1: # The skip budget
# A NEW SKIPPED TEST IS A CI REGRESSION unless it is written down here with a
# reason. A skip and a pass are printed two characters apart and exit the same
# way, so a gate that quietly stops evaluating anything looks exactly like one
# that evaluated everything and was satisfied. This repository has already been
# bitten by that at the job level -- a required check reported success in six
# seconds three times running -- and this is the same failure one level down.
# THREE STATES, and the third is the one budgets usually lack:
#   observed == expected   the skip is known and explained
#   observed >  expected   a NEW skip. Something stopped being checked.
#   observed <  expected   a STALE entry. The reason no longer holds, and an
#                          unmaintained budget becomes a graveyard of
#                          exceptions nobody re-reads. Fix the budget.
# TWO ENVIRONMENTS, because the honest count differs between them and pretending
# otherwise would make this fail on one machine or the other every time.
#   full   person-level artifacts present, as on a machine that ran the pipeline
#   lean   a bare checkout, which is what CI is
# The environment is detected from artifacts/amcb_npi_linkage_FROZEN.csv, which
# is gitignored by design and therefore the sharpest available signal.
# gate    path to the gate script
# kind    ci_skip   a gate that prints `  --   ` through ci_skip()
#         cycle     an adversarial-cycle test discovered by the glob step in
#                   ci.yml. It reports through have_inputs(), which prints the
#                   same `  --   SKIP` line ci_skip() does, so the same count
#                   works -- but nothing was watching them until the glob wired
#                   all 25 in and made their skips visible.
#         testthat  a file CI runs via testthat::test_file(), whose skips are
#                   reported as `[ FAIL n | WARN n | SKIP n | PASS n ]` and were
#                   invisible to this budget until 2026-08-29. A suite could
#                   convert every assertion into a testthat skip and the budget
#                   would still have said `Observed skips: 4`.
# when    pr      run and counted by the pull-request check
#         nightly declared but not run here, so the completeness check can see
#                 it without the PR tier paying for it
# full    expected skips with person-level artifacts present
# lean    expected skips on a bare checkout
# reason  why these skips are legitimate. An entry without one is a hiding place.
gate
column6: reason
